chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The time for the setting of the disk [of the sun] and the obligation of breaking the fast is that one stands facing the Qibla and observes the redness that rises from the East; when it passes the height of a man's head towards the West, then breaking the fast becomes obligatory and the disk has set.
ai.seo_question: How to determine the exact time for breaking the fast based on the setting of the sun?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the precise astronomical method for determining Maghrib time by observing the 'redness' (shafaq) rising in the East, a key indicator in Shia jurisprudence for the onset of evening prayer and breaking the fast. It emphasizes the necessity of facing the Qibla and tracking the redness's movement westward until it reaches the height of a person's head, signifying the sun's complete disappearance below the horizon. This practical guideline reflects the scholarly tradition of combining direct observation with specific celestial markers to ensure accurate timing for daily rituals.
